subject: how to check if covariates are significant using INLA

messages.author: bb0d51bd5af5ac0d
messages.subject: how to check if covariates are significant using INLA
parts:
Is there any built-in function in R-INLA that checks whether the covariates are necessary in the model? 

Also, when using default gaussian model in INLA, is it always better to scale the response to standard Normal? I noticed when I scale the response, the posterior mean looks much closer to the data(I used default setting of gaussian model). 

Thanks!

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] how to check if covariates are significant using INLA
parts:
AFAIK, the answer to your first question is no.

IMHO you should use sensible units for your response variable. Those units should match the magnitude of an expert's estimate of the response values. You express the distance between two cities in tens, hundreds or thousands of kilometers, not in meters. Let's assume that you use hundreds of km as a unit and measure the distance in meters. Then scale the response by a factor 1e5.
Doing this makes it much easier to interpret the model parameter as they in the same units as the response.

Best regards,

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] how to check if covariates are significant using INLA
parts:
Hi,

For the first question: Different interpretations of this goal gives very very different procedures. From p values to model comparisons.

For the second question: Scale everything to a reasonable scale always. Both responses and covariates. Whoever implemented the numerical algorithms you use (e.g. INLA) assume that you have reasonable numerical values everywhere. Any default settings assume you have "standard looking data".

Haakon
